title: Clicking something on a screen picks that thing, not the whole screen
goal: Once you drop a button onto a screen, clicking it selects the whole screen instead of the button, so moving it again or dragging it back off takes a double click first. Clicking a thing on a screen should pick that thing.
notes: Found while building screen adoption on 2026-09-03. The canvas rule today is EditorState.groupContextID: a click picks the outermost thing you are not already inside, so a frame swallows clicks aimed at its direct children. Figma treats top-level frames as click-through for their DIRECT children while ordinary groups still need a double click. See Scripts/playtest/screen-adoption-walk.json, stage steppedIn, which needs a double click to reach the rectangle it just dropped.
acceptance: A single click on a layer sitting directly on a screen selects that layer
A single click on the screen's empty surface still selects the screen
Dragging a layer straight off a screen needs no double click first
Layers inside an ordinary group still need a double click to reach, as they do today
